subject: USW-1: transient request-queue flattening and p95 elevation — customer update
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@heliotech.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliotech.com>
Cc: ops@heliotech.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: USW-1: transient request-queue flattening and p95 elevation — customer update

Hi Alex / Samir —

Wanted to proactively update you on a transient performance event that impacted hosted inference in our US-west (usw1) region this morning. Impact summary:

- What happened: we observed a sudden flattening in our initiation/request queue (shallow but wide fanout) which increased p95 generation latency for a subset of short-request workloads between ~07:50–08:05 PT.
- Scope: ~3% of requests for several hosted customers in usw1 saw p95 increases (rising from typical ~220ms to ~1.1s). Error rates did not materially increase, most requests were served with higher tail latency.
- Immediate mitigation: we rolled out targeted rate-smoothing on our front-line queue layer and enabled a conservative routing fallback to a low-cost model variant for affected request shapes. That change was applied at 08:02 PT and gradually reduced the p95 impact.

Attachments: initiation-queue-trend-20261109.png (png) — short time-series showing p50/p95 before/during/after.

We’re continuing a fast investigation; preliminary hypothesis is a coordinated traffic pattern from a small group of customers that produced many simultaneous short-window requests which amplified scheduling jitter in the initiation queue. We will:

- Continue collecting KV-cache and scheduler traces (team is on it).
- Publish a short follow-up with root cause and permanent fixes by EOD PT.
- Offer any support if you saw customer-facing symptoms — we can pull per-account traces if helpful.

Please confirm you received this and share if you saw client-side errors or unusual retry behavior.

Apologies for the disruption — we know tail latency matters for your workflows and are treating this as a high priority.

Best,
Soojin Lee

We saw a handful of increased response times on our side (timeouts are set to 1.5s; a few fell into the 1.1–1.4s range and triggered retries). No customer-facing errors were reported (retries masked most cases), but our backend observed a small spike in downstream call volume as a result.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you confirm whether any rate-limit headers or retry guidance needs to change for our integration?
2) Will you be sharing per-api-key traces/filters so we can correlate the spike with our internal telemetry?

If useful, I can share our inbound sample logs for the 07:45–08:15 PT window.

—Samir

Team — forwarding HelioHealth's quick reply. They captured retries on their side; they asked for per-api-key traces and whether retry guidance should change.

Preliminary notes from our side:
- Root cause hypothesis: bursty concurrent short requests (high concurrency, small payloads) exposed a scheduler batching inefficiency where many small windows were briefly starved, producing many outstanding initiations and widening the queue footprint ("flattening").
- Immediate mitigation already done: rate-smoothing + conservative model fallback (applied 08:02 PT).

Action items:
- Marissa / Ben: please pull per-api-key initiation traces for HelioHealth (api-keys: provided in the customer portal) for 07:40–08:20 PT and redact PII. Add trace links in this thread.
- Dev: validate whether a change in the front-line scheduler threshold (task aggregation window) would prevent reoccurrence; if safe, prepare a small patch/risk assessment.
- Evelyn: prepare a short customer-friendly postmortem doc & timeline we can share after we confirm root cause.

I'll follow up to HelioHealth with ETA for the traces and a short remediation plan.

Thanks —

Hi Alex / Samir — quick update with next steps and artifacts we can share: 

1) Traces and logs: Marissa attached per-api-key initiation traces (redacted) and a short graph (initiation-queue-trend-20261109.png). I also included a small patch we used to tune the scheduler smoothing threshold for the hot path (partial-rate-tuning.patch.txt) — this was deployed as a low-risk config tweak and removed the widened queue behavior in our canary cluster.

2) Why it happened (short): coordinated short bursts from a handful of API keys created many simultaneous initiation windows. Our scheduler aggregates work in fixed micro-windows; under certain concurrency shapes the aggregator produced many parallel windows instead of merging, which widened the queue and increased tail latency.

3) What we did: immediate rate-smoothing + fallback routing (08:02 PT), followed by a conservative scheduler threshold tweak (08:45 PT) rolled to canary and then region-wide. Both mitigations reduced p95 to ~270ms within ~20 minutes of the second change.

4) Next steps: 
- We're drafting a short postmortem and long-term fix (scheduler aggregation logic + a protective admission-control gate) — target publish: Tue EOD PT (2026-11-10).
- If you want, we can run a simulated traffic replay against your customer profile to validate no client-side changes are required; tell us a time window that works.

Links: status incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/USW-1-20261109
Postmortem draft (view only): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Qw_example_postmortem_link

Let me know if you want the raw logs; happy to pull additional slices. Thanks again for the rapid heads-up — the signal helped us narrow the scope quickly.
